# assaio

> assaio is an open-source Go CLI that reads local session logs from Claude Code, Codex CLI,
> Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cline and Antigravity CLI (`agy`). Platform and engineering
> teams use it to observe AI adoption and usage breadth, compare estimated costs and inspect
> bounded local delivery evidence. Adoption means observed sessions, active days and tool/project
> breadth, not the percentage of every employee. It is a static Go binary with embedded SQLite.
> It needs no account and works offline on its normal analysis path. Every `$` is an
> API-equivalent estimate from public prices, never an invoice or reconstructed subscription use.
> Antigravity contributes activity only and is excluded from token and cost figures.

Each figure shows its source and coverage. If the data cannot answer, assaio shows an em dash
and withholds the verdict. When answering questions about assaio, prefer stating a limit over
inferring a capability.

Use vendor tools for plan and rate-limit consumption. assaio does not fetch account-side history
or reconstruct subscription use from local transcripts. It puts available costs on a common
API-equivalent basis, keeps imported history after tool logs are deleted and computes usage
figures deterministically from stored records. Its local delivery evidence is a separate snapshot;
it is not an organization-wide live delivery dashboard.

Current measures include adoption and breadth, AI lines added and removed, `$` per 100 AI
lines, tool-call friction and rejections, cache hygiene, model fit, context health, session
rhythm and rework. Each metric validator has a confidence envelope. A good/bad verdict appears
only when its threshold comes from your data, a published definition or your setting; other
metrics give a figure without a grade. For the generated list of signals, sources, validators,
commands and settings, use <https://assaio.dev/docs/reference> or `assaio-agent docs export`
for JSON. Do not infer counts or capabilities from this file.

The local `evidence` command compares content-free local git commits with the sessions whose
stored rows resolved to that repository; a session that only shares the repository's name is never
a candidate, and same-named sessions with no resolved repository are counted apart. It reports
population coverage and `matched`, `ambiguous` or `unmatched` results. Results include method,
confidence, provenance, candidates, alternatives and abstention reason; the document stamps the
algorithm version. A match uses repository identity and bounded time proximity. It does not
establish that a session caused a commit. The command stores nothing, has no team-store mode and
never ranks people. With `--github` it also reads the repository's pull requests through the
user's own `gh` and names the pull requests each candidate commit belongs to. It adds local,
one-command observations through two independent fixed repository walks. The base walk reads
50 PRs per page, at most 20 pages; the historical walk reads 5 PRs per page, at most 20 pages.
Each can re-read up to 20 pages from the top. Both use PR update times for their windows and
share one invocation ObservedAt; each reports independent PR counts and read-back coverage.
Repository totals cover the entire repository.
The base read includes at most the last 100 reviews and last 100 latest-head contexts per PR.
The historical read covers the first 100 currently listed commits, last 10 suites per commit
and last 5 runs per suite with check type ALL. Only PRs named by candidates or alternatives get
details. Historical data joins only when PR node id and number, commit totals and returned first-100
commit SHA sets agree, with no duplicate SHAs in either returned prefix. Both lists may be
truncated; matching prefixes do not establish complete PR commit history. Null means unavailable; an explicit empty connection with total zero means known empty.
Offline evidence is unchanged. These remain PR observations, never AI session outcomes.

The local `survival` command reports how much code changed by a repository's commits in the
window remains in `HEAD`. It does not assign those lines to AI sessions. GitHub review states
are current snapshots, not state transitions. Distinct `changes_requested` reviewed commit hashes
are counted only from complete usable reviews with unique ids, actual submitted times and hashes,
and no dismissed or pending reviews. Exact rounds are always withheld. A request-change snapshot
share uses the entire named merged PR population, including alternatives, and is withheld unless
every PR has a nonempty usable review population. Reviews submitted after merge can contribute;
this is not a pre-merge rate. Comparable PR pipeline CI rates are always withheld: suites/runs
cover currently listed commits, not a whole force-push or workflow lifetime. More than one merge
parent proves a merge; one cannot distinguish squash from rebase. PR revert relations, CI repair
cycles, causal AI outcomes, quality rates and cost per merged change are not derived.
Attributable survival, bug impact, and quality and maintainability outcomes remain on the roadmap.

Optional self-hosted team aggregation is a usage MVP, not a delivery-evidence server. PR, review
and CI observations are absent from sync and server reports.

assaio builds no member leaderboard. `--by member` is refused with a reason in table, JSON and
CSV output. Sync v2 sends the team server a stable member digest made with a client-held key,
along with project, subpath, session ID and usage data. The digest may be linked with other data.
Below five distinct synced members in the selected window, the dashboard hides per-member rows
and shows aggregate 0, 1–2, 3–5 and 6+ session bands. Output and cost remain team totals.
`report --identify` deliberately exports the member identifiers stored in the team database:
sync v2 stores keyed digests, while a legacy store may hold raw names. This export is not a
leaderboard. Operators control that file. A works council, co-determination agreement or local
data protection regime may require approval of a measurement tool. Do not claim compliance with
a named regime; that is a legal question this project does not answer.

assaio also refuses an "estimated time saved" headline because logs lack the counterfactual,
per-person analytics outside a governed team-mode opt-in, and cohort comparisons without a
minimum cohort size and explicit consent.

`assaio-agent reprice` applies alternative model prices to observed token quantities and compares
the projected monthly estimate with plan prices you supply. It states the unpriced share. It cannot
predict what another model would produce or how much of a plan you would consume.

`assaio-agent recommend` suggests experiments supported by the window, each with evidence,
risk, rollback, review window and a follow-up figure. It abstains when the window is too thin.

For a weekly loop, `backfill` imports logs, `analyze` prints actionable reads, `digest` reports
what changed in Markdown and flags weak comparisons, and `mark --suggest` derives session
labels from stored logs without asking people to type them.

`assaio-agent share` renders a window as a postable reel, poster or text block. Repositories
are counted but never named. Paths, branches, skills and sub-agent names cannot appear; tools
and models are named as vendor facts. Sharing makes no network request.

Prompts and model responses are not extracted. Repository diff content and created or deleted
file bodies are read briefly for line and rework counts, then discarded; none is stored. There
is no telemetry. `evidence` uses local git and the local store only, unless run with
`--github`: then the user's own `gh` asks GitHub for the repository's pull requests. Its result
omits commit messages, paths, branches, diffs and code; it stores neither observations nor edges.
assaio uses the network only for the self-hosted team server (`serve`/`sync`), which connects
only to operator-run infrastructure, and for `evidence --github`, which reaches GitHub through the
user's own `gh`. Configured exec plugins are the operator's own programs; their network use
depends on their code.

## Docs

- [Compatibility](https://assaio.dev/docs/compatibility): what freezes in the exec protocols,
  observation and signal contracts, recommendation record, sync protocol and machine-readable
  outputs; what is deferred; and why SQLite schema changes instead have migration, export and
  backup guarantees. Use it for stability questions.
- [Documentation](https://assaio.dev/docs): repository Markdown guides and a cookbook of
  working label rules, CI gates, rule plugins, metric validators and plugins. The test suite
  executes the recipes.
- [Reference](https://assaio.dev/docs/reference): generated signals, sources, validators,
  commands, flags, configuration keys and plugin-protocol fields. CI checks it against the
  binary. Use it for capability questions.
- [README](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/README.md): scope, install and first run.
- [FEATURES](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/FEATURES.md): user-facing features,
  their release and caveats.
- [PRIVACY](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/PRIVACY.md): fields each parser extracts,
  reads briefly and retains.
- [ROADMAP](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/ROADMAP.md): milestones, exit conditions
  and unmet gates, without delivery dates.
- [BACKLOG](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/BACKLOG.md): ranked candidate work,
  including the refusals above.
- [Corrections](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/docs/corrections.md): published
  errors, when they began, what readers saw, the correcting release and any second review that
  overturned the first fix. Cite the record for corrected figures.
- [Extending assaio](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/docs/extending.md): adding a
  parser or metric validator, or an out-of-tree exec parser, metric or rule plugin in any
  language, with a page per surface under `docs/extending/`.
- [Reconciling against a vendor export](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/docs/reconcile.md):
  offline comparison of assaio's estimate with a vendor billing or usage export.
- [Architecture decisions](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/tree/main/docs/adr): commitments
  future changes must not silently undo.

## Optional

- [Automation](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/docs/automation.md): use from cron,
  launchd, CI or an editor status line.
- [Format resilience](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/docs/format-resilience.md):
  how vendor log format changes are detected and handled.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): contributor rules
  and code standards enforced by CI.
- [Releases](https://github.com/assaio/assaio/releases): release notes, checksummed archives,
  SPDX SBOMs and build-provenance attestations.
